articles.title: Kenan Thompson and Luis Guzman are hosting a New York gala for a charity fighting childhood brain cancer; the Cristian Rivera Foundation says it has donated over $4 million to research and family support
articles.summary: Actor and comedian Kenan Thompson and actor Luis Guzman were named among the hosts of the 17th Annual Cristian Rivera Foundation Celebrity Gala, a
articles.body: Actor and comedian Kenan Thompson and actor Luis Guzman were named among the hosts of the 17th Annual Cristian Rivera Foundation Celebrity Gala, a fundraising event scheduled for November 10 at Cipriani Wall Street in New York City. According to the foundation's official announcement, the organisation has donated more than $4 million towards research into diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG), a rare and aggressive childhood brain tumour, as well as financial assistance for affected families.The event, which also featured NBC's Darlene Rodriguez as a host, was organised to raise funds for clinical trials, medical research and family support programmes. The evening's programme was scheduled to include a red-carpet reception, dinner, an awards ceremony, live and silent auctions, and a video presentation highlighting the experiences of children and families affected by the disease.According to the foundation, proceeds from the gala will support research and clinical trials led by Dr Mark Souweidane at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center and Weill Cornell Medical College, along with research conducted by Dr Oren Becher at Mount Sinai Kravis Children's Hospital. A portion of the funds will also go towards providing direct financial assistance to families dealing with DIPG.Inspired by a lossThe organisation's origins are rooted in the personal tragedy of its founder, John "Gungie" Rivera, who established the Cristian Rivera Foundation in 2009 after losing his son to DIPG. According to the foundation's account, Cristian Alexander Rivera was diagnosed with an inoperable brain tumour on January 22, 2007. He was four years old at the time. Despite receiving treatment at Memorial Sloan Kettering and Weill Cornell Medical Center, the child died on January 25, 2009, after fighting the disease for two years.His father's experience prompted him to establish the New Jersey-based nonprofit with the aim of funding research towards a cure, spreading awareness and helping families navigate the challenges of a childhood cancer diagnosis. The foundation says it has since become one of the country's major private financial supporters of DIPG research. Its work also includes providing information, resources and monetary assistance to families affected by the disease.$365,000 donation supports research at Weill CornellIn January 2026, the organisation announced a $365,000 donation to Weill Cornell Medicine, its largest single contribution to date. According to a January 8 report by Weill Cornell Medicine, Thompson joined Rivera in presenting the donation to Dr Mark Souweidane, vice chair of the Department of Neurological Surgery and director of paediatric neurological surgery at NewYork-Presbyterian Komansky Children's Hospital.The contribution will support Souweidane's research into developing more effective, targeted treatments for children diagnosed with DIPG. The foundation said the donation was raised through its fundraising initiatives, including its annual celebrity gala.A February 2026 report by Inside Philanthropy also noted that the foundation had crossed the $4 million mark in cumulative donations towards DIPG research and family support.What is DIPG?DIPG is a fast-growing tumour that develops in the pons, a part of the brainstem responsible for several vital functions, including breathing, heart rate and movement. According to the US National Cancer Institute, approximately 300 children are diagnosed with the condition in the country every year.The tumour is particularly difficult to treat because of its location and its tendency to spread into surrounding healthy brain tissue. Most children diagnosed with DIPG do not survive longer than two years, the institute says. There is currently no established cure for the disease, making research into new treatment approaches and clinical trials particularly important.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: A Florida shipment declared as two terracotta pieces worth under $200 contained ancient Iraqi tablets valued above $15,000; a wider investigation has now forced the buyer to surrender artefacts and $75,000
articles.summary: A shipment arriving in Florida from the United Arab Emirates was declared to contain two terracotta objects worth less than $200.
articles.body: A shipment arriving in Florida from the United Arab Emirates was declared to contain two terracotta objects worth less than $200. But when US Customs and Border Protection officers inspected the package, they discovered two ancient Iraqi clay tablets dating back nearly 4,000 to 5,000 years and valued at more than $15,000 combined. The discovery triggered a wider investigation into suspicious antiquities shipments linked to Matthew Weinberg of Miramar Beach, Florida. According to a November 9 announcement by the US Department of Justice (DOJ), Weinberg has now forfeited multiple foreign antiquities and $75,000 to the federal government.The investigation began in July 2025, when agents from Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) were alerted by the Customs and Border Protection office in Pensacola about a shipment arriving at Pensacola International Airport from the UAE. The package was destined for Weinberg, and its shipping manifest described its contents as two terracotta objects valued at less than $200.However, an appraisal conducted after the shipment was detained identified the objects as cuneiform tablets originating from the region of modern-day Iraq. The tablets date to between 3000 BC and 2000 BC and were valued at more than $15,000 in total, according to prosecutors. Cuneiform is among the world's earliest known writing systems. Developed in ancient Mesopotamia, it involved pressing wedge-shaped marks into soft clay using a reed stylus. The writing system was used for recording everything from trade transactions and administrative records to literature, religious texts and royal accounts. The tablets offer a glimpse into civilisations that existed thousands of years ago in the region encompassing present-day Iraq.Investigation uncovers shipments from multiple countriesWhat initially appeared to be a single suspicious consignment led investigators to examine other international shipments linked to Weinberg. Federal authorities found that he had also obtained antiquities from Iran, Egypt and Cyprus, with their customs declarations similarly listing values significantly lower than the actual worth of the objects. These shipments included bronze figures, ceramic architectural models and terracotta idols. According to the DOJ, the imports violated restrictions that the United States had agreed upon with Iraq, Egypt, Cyprus and other countries to prevent the unauthorised movement of cultural property.The investigation subsequently expanded to Weinberg's residence in Miramar Beach. In March 2026, federal agents executed a search and seizure warrant at his home, recovering several additional objects, including ancient Hebrew Torah scrolls, scroll artwork originating from China and Egyptian antiquities dating to approximately 712 BC to 525 BC.A report by The Jewish Chronicle citing court filings and an affidavit, provided further details about the scale of the investigation. It reported that investigators identified approximately 117 international shipments associated with Weinberg's purchases between September 2024 and March 2026. Around 109 of these reportedly reached their destinations without being intercepted. The report also described a shipment containing a medieval Persian ceramic architectural model, which investigators believed Weinberg had purchased through eBay for approximately $2,000. Its declared shipping value was reportedly just $250.Investigators also reportedly discovered WhatsApp conversations between Weinberg and a vendor discussing ways to conceal the identities and values of antiquities to avoid customs detection. According to the report, searches on his phone also included queries about US laws governing the importation of Egyptian and Iraqi artefacts.Among the objects identified in the reported affidavit were a bronze figure depicting the Egyptian goddess Isis nursing Horus, an Iranian stone plaque featuring a scorpion and a terracotta female idol from Cyprus dating to approximately 1450 BC to 1200 BC.$75,000 forfeited, artefacts to be returnedFollowing the investigation, Weinberg forfeited the seized antiquities to the United States for repatriation to their countries of origin. He also surrendered $75,000 in US currency, which prosecutors identified as proceeds of violations of federal anti-smuggling statutes. The federal government has additionally barred him from purchasing or selling any foreign antiquities or artefacts for two years.US Attorney for the Northern District of Florida John P. Heekin said the recovered objects would be returned to their rightful owners and thanked federal law enforcement agencies for investigating violations of anti-smuggling laws.United States has entered into cultural property agreements with several countries to restrict the importation of certain archaeological and ethnological materials without appropriate documentation. These measures are intended to prevent objects from being removed from their countries of origin through unauthorised excavation, theft or trafficking.A previous high-profile case involved US retailer Hobby Lobby, which agreed in 2017 to forfeit thousands of ancient Iraqi artefacts that had been imported using misleading customs declarations. The objects included approximately 450 cuneiform tablets and 3,000 clay bullae. In 2018, the company agreed to pay $3 million as part of the settlement.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.summary: That night in Taipei wasn’t some secret rendezvous tucked away in a quiet corner of the city.
articles.body: That night in Taipei wasn’t some secret rendezvous tucked away in a quiet corner of the city. It was, by all accounts, just a standard tech-world night out - at least until social media got ahold of the photo months later.Back in June 2024, during the height of Computex buzz in Taiwan, Singaporean businesswoman Alice Huang was sitting at a Taipei bar alongside executives from companies like Gigabyte and NetThunder. Midway through the evening, the conversation turned to Nvidia's famous CEO. Alice casually dropped that she and Jensen were good friends and offered to ping him to see if he'd stop by.Sure enough, she sent a text, and Jensen actually showed up.Wearing his trademark black leather jacket, he pulled up a seat on a red velvet sofa, ordered a whiskey, and spent a bit of time talking shop and socializing with the group. A witness later mentioned that Jensen didn't stay long - he eventually called it a night, mentioned he was exhausted, and left the bar on his own.So why is a standard night of drinks from months ago suddenly blowing up online?The picture started making the rounds again recently because of a wave of internet chatter surrounding Jensen’s personal life and unverified claims about Alice herself. People online began dissecting the photo - Jensen in his jacket, Alice in a sleeveless top with a pearl necklace, sitting side by side - treating a public snapshot as if it were newly uncovered evidence.Some of the online noise has even tried linking Alice to Chinese intelligence, though it’s worth noting those rumors are completely unverified internet spec, not established facts. And despite sharing a last name, Alice and Jensen aren't related.Naturally, the sudden focus on the photo has led to extra scrutiny of Jensen’s long-standing personal life. He’s been married to his wife, Lori, since 1985. The two met decades ago as teenage lab partners in an electrical engineering class at Oregon State University, and Jensen has frequently credited her as his anchor throughout Nvidia’s rise.When you strip away the social media drama, the photograph itself doesn't prove anything beyond what actually happened: a high-profile CEO taking up an invitation to grab a quick drink with industry peers while in town for a major tech summit.

articles.title: Indian doctors are often mocked for saying 'gastroenterologist' differently; linguistics explains why they aren't wrong
articles.summary: Indian doctors have been mocked for decades over the way they say their own specialties. The linguistics says the mockery has it backwards.
articles.body: Indian doctors have been mocked for decades over the way they say their own specialties. The linguistics says the mockery has it backwards. Somewhere in an American hospital this morning, an Indian doctor is being corrected on the pronunciation of her own specialty. Slowly. The way you'd correct a child. She has been saying the word for nine years. She isn't saying it wrong.Listen to a resident in an OPD corridor in Chennai. Gas-tro-en-te-ro-lo-gist. Seven syllables, every one given its due, like beads counted off a string.Now listen to a consultant in Ohio. Gastro-en-tuh-ROL-uh-jist. Two syllables vanish into a mumble, one hammer blow lands on ROL, and everything else flattens out around it. Same word. Same spelling. Same Greek roots. Two completely different pieces of music, and only one of them ever gets called an accent.Why English eats syllablesEnglish runs a quiet rule on words ending in -ology. The stress goes on the linking o and nowhere else. Bi-OL-o-gy. Psy-CHOL-o-gy. Car-di-OL-o-gy. Four syllables or eight, the beat lands in the same place every time.The second half of that rule is the part nobody mentions. English is what linguists call stress-timed: the gaps between stressed beats stay roughly even, so whatever sits in between gets squeezed, and the vowels in those squeezed syllables lose their identity and collapse into a flat uh. The American version isn't seven syllables said quickly. It's one strong beat and five syllables starved of air on purpose.Indian English doesn't squeeze, and there are reasons. Start with the languages underneath. Hindi, Tamil, Bengali, Marathi, most of their neighbours, all syllable-timed. Every syllable gets roughly equal time and keeps its full vowel. No Tamil word has ever asked a speaker to starve a vowel, so nobody picked up the habit. Medical words are simply where you hear it most, because medical words are long.Then there's the fact that we can still see the joins. Anyone who sat through a Greekand-Latin roots lecture in second year knows gastro is stomach, entero is intestine, logist is one who studies. You say it in three blocks because that's what it is. The consultant in Ohio stopped seeing the seams years ago. He's saying one long noise he picked up by ear.And we learned it off the page. Indian medical English came out of Gray's and Davidson's, not out of conversation. Build a word from its spelling and you'll give every letter on that page a sound. A pronunciation taught by Indian teachers to Indian students for a hundred and fifty years, in a system with its own hospitals and its own examiners, isn't a mistake nobody caught. It's a dialect.Half of it isn't even IndianThis is the part that ought to settle the argument. A good deal of what Indians get corrected on in American hospitals isn't Indian at all. It's British, preserved intact, and the Americans are the ones who wandered off.An Indian registrar says an-JY-na, dyoo-OD-i-num, yoo-REE-ter, VIT-a-min. Her American colleague says AN-ji-na, doo-oh-DEE-num, YOOR-i-ter, VY-ta-min. On every one of those, London is with Delhi. She is saying the word the way her teacher's teacher learned it in Edinburgh. The people correcting her have just never heard it.The titles drift too. The doctor who puts you under is an anaesthetist here and in Britain, an anesthesiologist in America. Casualty is the emergency room. A house surgeon is an intern. And British surgeons, after all those years earning the title Doctor, hand it straight back on qualifying and go by Mr or Ms instead, a leftover from when surgeons were barbers, now worn as a badge. We kept Doctor for everybody, which is the sensible arrangement and much the duller one.What the smirking costsHaving insisted on every syllable, we then go and chop words in half in ways no hospital abroad would follow. You go to the gynic. Your cousin is doing ortho. Someone's son is a medico. The junior gets sent to medicine side. Nothing lazy about any of it. It's a working vocabulary, as quick as anything in London, and it travels badly only because nobody over there was taught it.India trains more doctors than any country on earth and sends them everywhere. They turn up fluent, examined in English, having read the same books as everyone in the room. And plenty of them spend their first couple of years quietly certain they sound uneducated, because somebody's eyebrow went up.That costs something real. It gets paid in confidence, in the half second of hesitation before speaking up on a ward round, in the registrar who decides not to argue with the consultant about a potassium. It buys nothing at all.No patient has ever come to harm from a fully pronounced gastroenterologist. If anything ours is the clearer version, every syllable audible, which counts for a lot when you're reading a drug name down a bad line at three in the morning.So the advice for anyone heading abroad isn't fix your accent. It's just this. Know the difference is there, so that a raised eyebrow reads as unfamiliarity rather than a verdict. And when you get home, go back to saying it our way. That's all it is. A way. Not an error on the road to becoming one.(By: Dr. Adit Mathur)You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ testGet the latest Lifestyle News and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Pakistan’s PTI demands access to jailed Khan after overnight hospital visit
articles.summary: Former Prime Minister Imran Khan ⁠is taken ⁠to a government hospital in Islamabad for treatment and returned to prison.
articles.body:
Islamabad, Pakistan – The party of jailed former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan has demanded access to its leader after he was taken to a hospital overnight for treatment and sent back to prison.

Khan, 74, briefly left the Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi for an eye examination at Islamabad’s Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS), the government hospital said on Wednesday.

In a statement, PIMS said a medical check was conducted on Khan on the advice of his ophthalmologist.

Khan has received a series of intravitreal injections in his right eye to treat central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO), a condition diagnosed after he reported reduced vision . He received his first injection in January.

PIMS said Khan received another injection overnight.

“His vital parameters were found to be normal. He was clinically stable, and his general physical examination was normal,” the hospital said, adding that he was discharged about 2:30am (21:30 GMT on Tuesday) with instructions for further care and follow-up.

Khan, a former cricket star who served as premier from 2018 to 2022, has been behind bars since August 2023 on multiple corruption charges he denies and calls politically motivated. The government rejects the allegation.

Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party on Wednesday said the overnight hospital visit and his return to his prison cell raise “deeply troubling questions” about his health, the quality of his medical care and the transparency surrounding his condition.

“A human being’s health is not a political bargaining chip. Nor can the medical treatment of a former prime minister be reduced to a procedural formality,” the PTI said, adding that the “state bears full responsibility for his safety and wellbeing”.

“His family, personal doctors and legal team must be given immediate and unrestricted access,” the party said.

PTI information secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram told Al Jazeera that Khan’s family and personal doctors were not told about the hospital visit and the party learned of it from news reports.

“No one from the family or party was there [at the hospital]; our personal physician was not there either,” he said.

During a hearing on Tuesday, Khan’s lawyer Salman Safdar told the Islamabad High Court that while Khan had said his eyesight had improved, his blood pressure remained a concern.

Safdar had appeared on behalf of Khan and his wife, Bushra Bibi, to appeal against their convictions in a property case.

In response, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry told reporters that Khan was receiving the required medical care and his treatment was not being neglected.

In August, the Supreme Court ordered that Khan should be moved to a private hospital of his choice in Islamabad. Instead, he was taken to PIMS and returned to jail .

articles.title: Democrats and Republicans unite to investigate Nvidia, but diverge on whether Trump is at fault
articles.summary: Republicans and Democrats are showing rare unity in their calls for investigations into whether Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang compromised U.S. national security after admitting he had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The revelation surfaces a host of concerns that cut across committees related to intelligence, foreign relations and banking and finance, diving deep…
articles.body:
Republicans and Democrats are showing rare unity in their calls for investigations into whether Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang compromised U.S. national security after admitting he had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

The revelation surfaces a host of concerns that cut across committees related to intelligence, foreign relations and banking and finance, diving deep into the relationships between China, the U.S. and Huang, the head of the largest U.S. chipmaking company producing the most advanced technology surrounding artificial intelligence.

While there’s bipartisan concern over whether the Chinese government and military accessed Nvidia’s most advanced chips and technology, Democrats are likely to be more focused on what President Trump knew and when.

“That’s central,” Sen. Chris Coons (D-Del.) told The Hill.

Coons, likely the incoming chair of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee when Democrats assume the majority in January, is pushing for an investigation into the relationship between Trump and Huang.

He wanted to know why Trump ignored reported intelligence briefings that Huang was in a relationship with a suspected Chinese asset.

“Why did he put our national security at risk? Why did he take Jensen Huang with him on Air Force One, to significant meetings with the Chinese? … That strikes me as the most pressing question,” he continued.

Trump, at the last minute, brought Huang on board Air Force One to travel to Beijing in May — after Secretary of State Marco Rubio informed him the U.S. had sensitive intelligence that the Nvidia CEO was in a relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, The New York Times reported.

Trump said Monday that any intelligence presented to him “didn’t make much of an impact on me” when asked about the news at the White House.

“I’ve got a lot of questions,” Sen. Mark Warner (D-Va.), the ranking member of the Senate Intelligence Committee, said Tuesday when asked about whether there will be a briefing for the full Senate.

Warner said he’s not sure which committee would take the lead on an investigation.

“There’s lots of jurisdictions between an awful lot of committees. Intelligence, my committee, has a huge footprint there. There are questions in terms of export controls, which come out of Banking,” he said.

Outgoing Sen. John Cornyn (R-Texas) did not address a question on whether he has concerns about Trump’s relationship with Huang but said he wanted a probe into reports the Commerce Department approved chip sales to alleged shell companies with ties to the Chinese military.

“I don’t know yet, sort of, who was instrumental in those decisions. And that’s why I think there needs to be an investigation to figure out what exactly happened,” Cornyn told The Hill.

The Texas senator is a member of the Senate Intelligence Committee and the Foreign Relations Committee but lost his seat after Trump backed his GOP primary competitor.

Cornyn questioned why Huang didn’t receive a “defensive briefing by the FBI” to alert him that he was the subject of a foreign intelligence operation.

“That’s typically what happens in counterintelligence investigations. You tell the target of the intelligence operation, ‘Hey this is not an innocent interaction, this is a nation state spying on you and our country,’” he said.

The FBI declined to comment to The Hill.

Cornyn’s remarks echo Republicans’ concerns over Huang and whether he compromised U.S. national security, but they are stopping short of questioning Trump’s actions.

Three House Republicans have called for Huang to come before them for a closed-door briefing on Nvidia’s security protocols and his “interactions with a publicly reported People’s Republic of China (PRC) intelligence asset: Megaspeed executive Alice Huang.”

There’s no familial relation between the two. Jensen Huang has admitted to having an extramarital affair and said Nvidia’s board of directors is launching an independent investigation into the national security concerns.

Republicans critical of Huang’s longtime push to allow Nvidia to sell its chips to China have used the scandal to advocate for passing bipartisan legislation to tighten export controls.

Sens. Jim Banks (R-Ind.) and Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) issued a call to pass their bill, the AI Overwatch Act, to cut off pathways for China to access advanced chips.

Likewise, Rep. Brian Mast (R-Fla.) called for AI export-control bills to ensure “China can never get their hands on our most advanced technology.”

“This situation with NVIDIA’s CEO is a massive concern for the national security of the United States,” he posted on the social platform X.

Mast said he had no concerns over Trump’s relationship with Huang when asked Tuesday evening by The Hill.

Democrats are also concerned about the Commerce Department’s actions. Three senior Democrats on the House Foreign Affairs Committee are demanding Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick halt exports of advanced AI chips.

“We hope that the Department did not ignore warnings about a suspected PRC intelligence operation while allowing advanced American technology to flow through companies under scrutiny,” they wrote in a letter sent Monday .

“If Commerce was not briefed, we need to know why. If it was briefed, we need to know how it responded. And if the Department knowingly permitted these exports despite credible national-security concerns, the American people deserve an explanation.”

articles.title: Suspected bomb threat hoaxes prompt evacuation of Italian schools, alarm in UK and Ireland
articles.summary: Hundreds of schools across Italy were evacuated on Wednesday after bomb threats were sent to about 6,300 institutions, becoming the latest in a series of incidents targeting infrastructure across Europe.
articles.body: Hundreds of schools across Italy were evacuated on Wednesday after bomb threats were sent to about 6,300 institutions, becoming the latest in a series of incidents targeting infrastructure across Europe. Schools in Scotland, Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland also received emails Wednesday, although police warned these were likely hoaxes and education facilities were not evacuated. Italian police told CNN that hundreds of schools in the country were evacuated. Officials later said that the incident was a suspected hoax. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said in a statement that there was currently no indication that a “concrete danger exists.” Meloni said the government was “following very closely” reports of the threats directed at schools, saying the incidents appeared aimed at “generating alarm and concern.” Authorities were investigating the source of the email, the police spokesperson said, declining to confirm the email address the communication came from. About 6,300 schools across Italy received the e-mail threat, a spokesperson for the Italian public education ministry told CNN Wednesday. “It’s unclear how many have been evacuated, that is a decision taken locally under the advice of local authorities,” the spokesperson added. In central Rome, dozens of kindergarten and primary school children enjoyed a day off as the Quirinio Visconti primary school was evacuated. Their parents were notified to pick them up, a teacher told CNN. The Italian prime minister said the government was “doing everything necessary to ensure the safety of citizens.” Schools in UK and Ireland also receive emails In Northern Ireland, more than 300 schools received a threatening email, police said Wednesday, adding that the message originated outside the United Kingdom and was being treated as a hoax. “Our enquiries are ongoing, however, at this stage we consider risk to the public as low,” Assistant Chief Constable Anthony McNally said in a statement. The Education Authority said the message sent to “a large number of schools” in Northern Ireland resembled a hoax sent to schools last month and that it was unaware of any evidence of a “credible” threat. Police in the Republic of Ireland said a generic communication was sent to “a number of educational establishments” Wednesday. Police assessed the threat as “not credible” and said they were not advising any evacuations. Dublin teacher Sharon Magee told CNN her school received a bomb threat at 10:55 a.m. local time (5:55 a.m. ET), but it was not evacuated. “We were just told to keep alert in case we noticed anything on the premises and then the day just went ahead as normal,” she said, adding that everyone at the school got through the day safely. Meanwhile, Police Scotland said “threatening messages” were sent to schools. The force said the messages were being treated as hoaxes and advised schools that the emails alone did not warrant evacuation. Wave of disruption across Europe Wednesday’s incident is the latest in a series targeting infrastructure and organizations across Europe. “Everyone can be a target and that makes it harder to defend ourselves 100%,” Italian Defense Minister Guido Crosetto told CNN the day before hundreds of schools were evacuated Wednesday, describing efforts by Italian authorities to combat attacks. “The goal of this hybrid warfare is to destroy this sovereignty and generate panic,” Crosetto said. Last week, a string of hoax bomb threats disrupted dozens of flights and targeted media organizations across the continent. And in the last few weeks, cyberattacks have hit supermarket refrigeration systems in France, Sweden, Belgium and Ireland. The European Union said last week it was too early to tell whether the bomb threat incidents were linked, while security analysts and government ministers have suggested the wave could be part of a wider hybrid campaign or series of malicious hoaxes. This story has been updated with developments.

articles.body: At least 10 police personnel, including two senior officers, were killed in a militant attack in Pakistan's northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province on Wednesday, officials told news agency AP.The attack occurred in Kohat district, where militants targeted vehicles carrying police officers, leading to an exchange of gunfire between the attackers and security forces, local police official Faisal Khan said.Khan confirmed that two senior police officers were among those killed. He added that the gunbattle was still underway, but did not share further details.No militant organisation has claimed responsibility for the attack so far. However, suspicion is likely to centre on the Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), also known as the Pakistani Taliban, which has intensified its attacks on security forces in the region in recent months.Pakistan has witnessed a rise in militant violence over the past few years, with much of it attributed to the TTP. The group is separate from the Afghan Taliban but shares close ties with it. The Afghan Taliban returned to power in Afghanistan in 2021.Islamabad has repeatedly accused Afghanistan's Taliban-led government of providing shelter to TTP fighters operating against Pakistan. articles.title: Reform boycotts Senedd after member banned for saying white people being replaced
articles.summary: Party members withdrew from most of Wednesday's Senedd proceedings over Joe Martin's speaking ban.
articles.body:
Reform UK will partially boycott the Senedd to protest the ban of one of their politicians for claiming white people are being "replaced".

The party's Welsh leader, Helen Jenner, said Joe Martin's ban was because of "undue pressure" from governing party Plaid Cymru and was an "infringement on freedom of speech".

Martin had been told he would not be allowed to speak in the Senedd's chamber until he apologised for the remarks, which the parliament's Presiding Officer Huw Irranca-Davies called "unnecessarily provocative and deliberately offensive".

Reform UK leader Nigel Farage called the ruling "ridiculous and outrageous".

Reform, which is by far the Senedd's largest opposition party, said its members would withdraw from most of Wednesday's proceedings before returning to vote in the parliament later in the evening.

Reform's Joe Martin given Senedd speaking ban after he said white people are being replaced

Jenner confirmed her party's boycott on the steps of the Senedd on Wednesday afternoon.

"It is now clear that the freedom of speech of one of our Senedd members is being curtailed, meaning his constituents are being silenced," she said.

"We stand behind Joe, and we will not attend today's plenary session in protest at his treatment.

"Every Reform MS [Member of the Senedd] will be in their Senedd office working hard for our constituents."

"My voters sent me to the Senedd to speak on their behalf," he said.

"I am being blocked from doing so, and now it's clear that I have fewer rights than the people who elected me. That cannot be the situation in a national parliament."

Asked by BBC Wales if he genuinely believed white people were being "replaced" in the UK, Martin said: "That's obviously a fact."

Posting on X, Farage said it was "ridiculous and outrageous that Reform's duly elected Member of the Senedd, Joe Martin, has been banned from speaking in the Welsh Parliament".

"Why is it only Reform that's targeted like this?" he asked.

Martin was also backed by the leader of right-wing party Restore Britain, Rupert Lowe.

He called for the Senedd to be "shut down" if it was "going to shut down legitimate debate around demographic security and immigration".

Martin's Caerdydd Penarth constituency includes some of Wales' most ethnically diverse communities.

On Tuesday Martin asked for a Welsh government statement on the "demographic replacement of white British people" during business questions, when Senedd members are free to raise issues they choose.

Business Minister Heledd Fychan immediately asked the presiding officer whether the remarks were within the Senedd's standing orders - a set of rules that govern conduct in the chamber.

Standing orders give the presiding officer discretion to decide if contributions to plenary sessions - meetings of the full Senedd - use "discriminatory or offensive language".

Delivering his ruling later, Irranca-Davies said: "Until I receive a clear indication that the member understands the boundaries of acceptable parliamentary conduct and apologises to the Siambr [chamber], we will not be calling him to speak."

Senedd officials confirmed an apology would have to be made in the chamber during a plenary session.

Martin is a member of the Senedd's Equality, Human Rights and Social Justice Committee.

Irranca-Davies pointed out it was not the first time he has rebuked Martin. In September, he said Martin had made offensive remarks about surgeons working in the Welsh NHS gender service .

Plaid Cymru Senedd member Carrie Harper called Reform's boycott a "pathetic tantrum" that was a "disgrace to democracy".

"They'd rather play gimmicks and chase headlines than be serious about Wales' future and doing the job they were elected to do on behalf of the people they represent," she said.

In the 2021 census 93.8% of people in Wales identified as white, down from 95.6% a decade earlier, with the country's overall population growing by 1.4% to 3,107,500.

The proportion identifying as Asian, Asian Welsh or Asian British, the next highest group in the survey, rose from 2.3% to 2.9%.

Mixed or multiple ethnic groups rose from 1% to 1.6%, and those identifying as Black, Black Welsh, Black British, Caribbean or African rose from 0.6% to 0.9%.

articles.title: U.S. on verge of losing measles-free status and Democrats brace for Stephen Miller clashes: Morning Rundown
articles.summary: An NBC News investigation reveals childhood vaccination rates are dropping as measles cases surge.
articles.body: An NBC News investigation reveals childhood vaccination rates are dropping as measles cases surge. Democrats skeptical about working with new White House chief of staff Stephen Miller. And Russia’s top independent newspaper shuts down after more than two decades. Here’s what to know today. U.S. on the verge of losing measles-free status as cases surge Should the U.S. lose its measles elimination status? That’s what public health experts expect will be the outcome of a meeting this week of an independent commission of the Pan American Health Organization. The group of eight people is made up of epidemiologists, infectious disease and vaccine experts from countries in the Americas. This is Morning Rundown, a weekday newsletter to start your day. Sign up here to get it in your inbox. If the U.S. loses elimination status, it will join Canada as the only other country in the region to have lost control of the virus, paving the way for illnesses and deaths. The milestone would also mark a stunning reversal of efforts to stop the spread of the world’s most contagious disease. In 2000, there were only about 100 confirmed cases in the entire country. This year, there have been more than 5,000 confirmed cases and 43 new outbreaks across the country. Eight people, including four babies too young to be vaccinated, have died. An updated NBC News/Stanford University analysis reveals an alarming drop in childhood vaccination rates, particularly in the country’s most vulnerable areas. In hard-hit Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, the share of kindergarteners who got MMR vaccines in 2025-26 was 87.6%, compared to 95.5% before the pandemic. An immunization rate of 95% is needed to prevent the spread of measles. The country’s immunity was eroded by decades of scientifically dubious claims about the dangers of childhood vaccines, and misinformation then exploded during the pandemic. Read the full story here. More from The Vaccine Divide: See maps of vaccination rates in your county and where exemption rates in schools are rising. Learn more about how NBC News gathered and analyzed the data. Stephen Miller’s elevation sends a message to Dems President Donald Trump signaled he might be willing to work with Democrats on his priorities after last week’s election results. But his decision to oust Susie Wiles and install Stephen Miller as White House chief of staff has left some Democratic lawmakers pessimistic. Rep. Hakeem Jeffries, who is expected to become House speaker, said he has “zero interest” in working with Miller, calling him a “stone-cold racist.” Rep. Jamie Raskin said Miller, the face of hard-line immigration enforcement, “might not be able to engage in any kind of course correction.” Democrats have recoiled at Miller’s elevation, expecting blanket opposition to the bills they pass and the oversight investigations they plan to launch. articles.title: A Swiss heart surgeon has reclaimed her Guinness World Records title with 3,200 heart-shaped objects; Diana Reser has spent 25 years collecting everything from artwork to household items
articles.summary: Diana Reser tends to hearts by day. She is one of Switzerland’s leading cardiac surgeons. In her spare time, she collects them.
articles.body: Diana Reser tends to hearts by day. She is one of Switzerland’s leading cardiac surgeons. In her spare time, she collects them. Her collection of heart-shaped objects now numbers 3,200, enough to reclaim the Guinness World Records title she lost in 2024.It all started with a presentDiana Reser’s obsession with hearts started around 25 years ago, when she was a medical student. She had just finished an internship in heart surgery and knew she wanted to pursue that career. When word got around, she began receiving presents. Friends, colleagues and patients sent her heart-shaped things. She has been collecting hearts ever since. About half of her current collection was gifted to her. She tracked down the rest herself, from places all over the world.All things heartAsk for any object you might need, and Diana Reser would ask if you would like it in the shape of a heart. “You name it, I have it. Basically everything you can use in your everyday life,” she told the organisers. She has heart-shaped solar lights, car air fresheners, hair accessories, perfume bottles, soap and jewellery. Her home and office also house a heart-shaped Rubik’s Cube, a working stethoscope and even a fragment of the Berlin Wall. There are also two paintings. One is a Picasso-style canvas of three women holding a heart. The other is a barn owl with a heart-shaped face, painted by her sister. And her heart collection does not end at the front door. Reser even has six heart tattoos!Making it into the Guinness World RecordsDiana Reser first set the Guinness World Records title in 2010 with 775 items. In 2024, the title passed to a collector in the United States, Susan West, whose collection of heart-shaped containers was certified that February. Reser never felt she had truly lost the title. She knew her own collection was bigger. She simply hadn’t gone through the paperwork again.But this April, she decided to give it a second try. She sorted all 3,200 items into categories and submitted the count. Two witnesses, Peter Hartmeier and Ralph Pöhner, confirmed that the collection exists. Reser is careful about the numbers. She cannot control what people give her, so she welcomes each new piece, even when she already owns something similar.“For the record attempt I categorised all 3,200 hearts I possess and you can certainly say that the counts are very high – but I just can’t influence what people give me for presents, and therefore I am happy about every new piece, no matter how many I already have of the same or similar kind,” the cardiac surgeon told the organisers.Why is she so fond of hearts? Diana Reser tries to answer this as an ordinary woman rather than a cardiac surgeon. “The fascination of heart surgery and the strong presence of the heart shape in our everyday lives [is what drew me to hearts]. It is a universal symbol for love, life and the soul.”She also has a name for the effect: heart-itis. It is, by her account, contagious. “It is curious, but once you consciously see hearts in your environment you won’t unsee them ever again. I call this ‘heart-itis’. It is contagious and once you are infected, you will never get rid of it.”Reser dedicates this unusual feat to her family. “I dedicate my collection to them and to raising awareness of everyone’s own heart health. We can do so much nowadays to prevent, detect and treat heart disease before it is too late. Everybody should go for a heart check-up at 50 at the latest, or earlier if there is a history of heart disease in the family. And if you really need heart surgery, it is not the end of the world: don’t be afraid of it, because it is a very safe surgery in elective patients.”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Israel faces political chaos as Netanyahu’s grip on power weakens. What will it take to end the disarray?
articles.summary: Netanyahu lost the parliamentary majority that kept him in power over the past four years and his rival Gadi Eisenkot faces a difficult task in unseating him.
articles.body: The wheels of Israel’s political machine are turning. But that doesn’t mean they’re going anywhere soon. In the latest elections, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu lost the parliamentary majority that kept him in power over the past four years. But his main rival, Gadi Eisenkot, still faces a difficult task in unseating Israel’s longest-serving leader after being tasked with forming the next government. On paper, Eisenkot has a clear majority, with 67 of 120 seats in Israel’s legislature, the Knesset. But those seats come from six ideologically diverse parties, from right-wing to Arab parties. That’s the challenge that Eisenkot, a neophyte politician, must address as he aims for the premiership: how to make these parties cooperate to both support him and help him govern. For decades, Netanyahu commanded the loyalty of the political parties within his bloc. Even if they challenged him, he was adept at managing the disagreements and holding his coalition together. Eisenkot has no such experience, and though he has veteran politicians within his bloc, he must now find a way to lead them toward a common goal: forming a government to replace Netanyahu. How is a government normally formed? In most elections in Israel – and in just about any parliamentary democracy – one party emerges with the clear backing of a majority of the parliament. In Israel’s Knesset, that amounts to at least 61 out of 120 seats. The leader of that party becomes the prime minister. After the 2022 election, Netanyahu emerged with 64 seats. He then gained four more seats when an additional party joined his coalition. That gave him a commanding 68-seat majority, and the government lasted its entire term for the first time since 1988. Netanyahu now has only 46 lawmakers supporting him, leaving him far short of the majority needed to govern. Eisenkot has 67 seats backing him, but it gets complicated because not all of those parties have agreed to work together. Could Israel get a government that doesn’t have a parliamentary majority? The election produced a complicated deadlock, leaving neither side with a clear path to forming a government. Netanyahu’s 53-seat pre-election bloc shrank to 46 seats in the 120-seat Knesset after United Torah Judaism, an ultra-Orthodox party long loyal to the prime minister, declined to support him. The opposition won 67 seats, but 19 of those belong to the two Arab parties – the Joint List and Raam. That makes them pivotal to any attempt to replace Netanyahu. However, many Jewish Israelis, including some of those opposed to Netanyahu, do not consider the Arab parties to be legitimate partners. Still, the Arab parties could support what’s called a minority government from the outside, providing it with a parliamentary safety net. A minority government holds fewer than the 61 parliamentary seats needed to support a stable coalition but remains in power after securing the backing of Knesset members who don’t sit in the cabinet. Israeli law requires only a simple majority to install a government, so a government can take office if its opponents are divided and abstain from voting. Removing one is harder: It requires a constructive majority of more than half the lawmakers who support an alternative government. Gadi Eisenkot’s plan is to form what he calls a “national emergency government”: a minority government made of the four Jewish opposition parties, which together hold 48 seats: his own Yashar, Together – led by former prime ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid; Avigdor Liberman’s Yisrael Beiteinu, and the left-wing Democrats, led by Yair Golan. The Arab parties wouldn’t be part of the coalition but would guarantee majority parliamentary support to keep it in power, in exchange for various concessions. Israel has had minority governments in the past, but never immediately after an election. Yitzhak Rabin’s second government became a minority government after the ultra-Orthodox Shas party left his coalition in 1993. The government survived two more years with support from outside Arab parties. Another possible variable is seeking the support of United Torah Judaism (UTJ), an ultra-Orthodox party. Though it is a traditional ally of Netanyahu, the party refused to recommend him during the post-election presidential consultations, opening a possibility that it could abstain from voting or even support an Eisenkot-led minority government, widening his safety net beyond the Arab parties. But it would likely demand concessions from Eisenkot. Who is blocking Eisenkot’s plan and could the ultra-Orthodox parties become kingmakers? Eisenkot’s main obstacle now is Avigdor Liberman. The former minister of defense, foreign affairs and finance refuses to join any government dependent on the Arab parties, arguing that a minority government will be short-lived and will only strengthen Netanyahu. Instead, he is proposing a different route: a 61-seat coalition that includes the ultra-Orthodox parties and excludes the Arab parties. He believes that once it is formed, some lawmakers from Netanyahu’s Likud party could defect. Liberman has dropped his longstanding veto on the ultra-Orthodox parties, but his plan collides with one of the opposition’s core commitments: ending the blanket draft exemption for ultra-Orthodox men from mandatory military service. The ultra-Orthodox parties want to entrench that exemption, while Eisenkot, Liberman and others campaigned for universal service. Any deal would require a major ideological concession, and still appears distant, as Shas remains loyal to Netanyahu, even as UTJ signals an opening. Liberman’s strategy risks undermining Eisenkot’s minority-government route, but the two are coordinating their next moves. Even before forming a government, the opposition plans to use its parliamentary majority to take control of the Knesset by replacing Netanyahu’s appointed speaker and other parliamentary officeholders, then begin advancing legislation. Could Eisenkot and Netanyahu share power in a unity government? Netanyahu has been applying heavy pressure against any Jewish-Arab political cooperation. In recent days, he has released two videos calling for a “national unity government.” But he only wants it on his terms: he insists on remaining prime minister and including his entire right-wing and ultra-Orthodox bloc. Unity governments are traditionally formed by Israel’s two largest parties following a political deadlock. After the 1984 elections, Labor’s Shimon Peres and Likud’s Yitzhak Shamir famously governed together and shared the premiership under a rotation agreement. After the 1988 elections, they joined forces again. Netanyahu has also led two such arrangements recently. In 2020, during the Covid crisis and after three inconclusive elections, Benny Gantz joined him for an emergency government. Gantz was supposed to take over and become prime minister after 18 months. But Netanyahu looked for a way out before stepping aside, forcing new elections by refusing to pass a state budget. After the October 7, 2023 attack, Gantz and Eisenkot joined a war cabinet. The two resigned after eight months, citing frustration with Netanyahu’s handling of the Gaza war and lack of strategy. Eisenkot has rejected Netanyahu’s national unity rhetoric as a “pathetic spin.” If Netanyahu genuinely wants to cooperate, he said, he should break with his extremist partners and join a government led by Eisenkot. While Netanyahu appears unwilling to separate from his entire bloc, some analysts believe he may eventually be willing to part ways with National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir, but not with Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich and the ultra-orthodox parties. So far, he has given no indication he would make such a concession, and the opposition sees his unity appeals mainly as a tactic to undermine a government that could replace him. Can Netanyahu still hold on? For now, he remains in office as caretaker prime minister until a new government is sworn in. Eisenkot has 28 days from last Sunday to negotiate with his bloc over cabinet posts, budgets and policies. He can ask for a 14-day extension. If he fails, the mandate passes to another candidate for 28 days. If Netanyahu gets the mandate, he will likely try to lure a party or individual lawmakers from the opposition to join his bloc. Eisenkot, Bennett, Liberman, and Golan have all declared they will not join him. With his bloc eight seats short, Netanyahu would need eight individual defectors, setting a high bar. But time is on his side. If he fails, the mandate returns to the Knesset for another 14 days to try and suggest another candidate. If that fails as well, the political deadlock will lead Israel to another round of elections. During that period, Netanyahu would remain as caretaker prime minister.

articles.title: Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi end with prisoner exchange agreement
articles.summary: The talks in the UAE capital were the first ⁠between the two warring sides since February.
articles.body:
Two days of talks between Russian and Ukrainian officials, mediated by the United States, have yielded agreement on a prisoner exchange but failed to make a breakthrough on ending the war, which is nearing the five-year mark.

Russia’s chief ⁠⁠negotiator, Vladimir Medinsky, said at the talks ⁠⁠in the United Arab Emirates capital, Abu Dhabi, on Wednesday that both sides had agreed on a large-scale prisoner swap and that mutual understanding ⁠⁠had been achieved on some issues.

Russia’s state-run news agency TASS reported that the prisoner exchange should happen in two to three weeks. If finalised, it would be the latest in a ⁠long line of such ⁠exchanges.

US envoy Jared Kushner told a news conference the number of prisoners would be finalised on Thursday. He added that he would travel to Moscow alongside US special envoy Steve Witkoff to relay what was discussed to Russian President Vladimir Putin and “make more progress on some of the issues that were discussed, because we see some openings and some opportunities there”.

Kushner and Witkoff are then scheduled to fly to Dublin, Ireland, to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy “and explore some of the ideas we came up with”.

Political analyst Dmitry Medvedenko told Al Jazeera that prisoner exchanges have been a regular occurrence without this level of diplomatic work. “Every two or three months you have 100 to 300 prisoners exchanged by both sides; this is a channel that actually works,” he said.

Ukraine and Russia freed 200 prisoners of war each in March following talks in Geneva , Switzerland, in February. Last year, they each exchanged 146 prisoners after mediation by the UAE, and large-scale prisoner exchanges followed three rounds of talks in Istanbul, Turkiye, from May to July.

“For it to be the biggest prisoner exchange, it should top the 1,000-for-1,000 exchange in May last year,” Medvedenko said.

The two warring sides entered Wednesday’s talks far apart on terms for a possible settlement to the war.

Kushner said it was “a long way to get everyone back to the table” and that “this was a very tough meeting but a productive one”. He added that territorial issues would be the hardest to settle but that “progress” was made on a post-war security framework.

Medinsky said more talks would be held in the near future and that Moscow was not opposed to participation from the European Union. He added, however, that it was ⁠unclear what there ⁠was for Russia and the EU to discuss, given what he ‌said was a lack of proposals from the European ‌side.

Ukraine’s peace negotiator David Arakhamia said there was “good ⁠momentum” from peace talks in Abu Dhabi towards ‌reaching a solution before the end of the year and that the next talks should be multilateral, ‌not trilateral, adding that Europe should ‌be ‌represented.

Zelenskyy, who, like Putin, is not attending the talks, said on Wednesday he did not think it was possible to think about European security “without Europe”.

Kushner said further talks with the Russian and Ukrainian presidents would touch upon “whether we can get Europeans to the format and make this a multilateral format”.

articles.title: Schools across Italy evacuated after receiving email bomb alerts
articles.summary: Italian PM Meloni says there is no danger as UK and Northern Ireland authorities also report ‘bogus’ alerts.
articles.body:
Schools across Italy have been evacuated after about 6,300 of them received the same hoax bomb threat by email, while authorities in Scotland and Northern Ireland also reported receiving similar alerts.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni stressed on Wednesday that there was no indication of any concrete danger to Italian schools, but investigations were under way, and a meeting of government ministers has been convened.

The email also included a threat to Meloni and was reportedly signed by “Mikhail Andropov, leader of the Vilayat of ⁠⁠⁠⁠Misoginistan”, according to the Reuters news agency, citing a copy of the message it obtained.

The same purported author claimed responsibility for email bomb threats sent on Friday to newsrooms in Ireland and Bulgaria.

Wednesday’s security alert came amid rising concerns ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠in Europe about hybrid warfare threats , which have targeted supermarkets, blood banks, air traffic and TV broadcasters.

Italian Education ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌Minister Giuseppe Valditara told the La7 TV channel that at least 300 schools were affected by the bomb threats, adding that the number could rise.

“It is clear that there is a strategy at play,” he told the network. “It is difficult to say right now who might be behind this. Intelligence services are, of course, working to identify them.”

But he added: “There is no need for alarmism as the content of the emails makes it clear that any concrete risk is virtually nonexistent. In all likelihood, this is a cyberattack rather than a genuine threat.”

‘Bogus’ threats in Northern Ireland and Scotland

Separately on Wednesday, ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠a ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠large number of schools in Scotland and Northern Ireland ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠were also sent threatening emails. The Northern Ireland Education Authority said schools there have been advised to stay open because police ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠did not regard them ⁠⁠⁠⁠as a credible threat.

“The message has ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠similarities with a ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠bogus threat ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠sent last month, which was declared a hoax ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌by PSNI [Police Service of Northern Ireland],” the Education Authority said.

Police Scotland also said the messages sent to schools in that country do not represent a credible threat and are being treated as hoaxes. The police force said its cyber and fraud unit is working to establish the source of the messages, liaising with law enforcement across the United Kingdom and internationally.

This follows a similar mass bomb hoax email sent to Scottish schools on October 19.

This month, flights across Europe have been diverted, grounded and escorted by fighter jets in response to a wave of bomb threats.

There have also been cyberattacks on supermarkets in several European cities, with hackers changing the temperature on refrigeration in an apparent attempt to spoil food.

Last week, hackers raised the temperatures of refrigeration systems at supermarkets in Germany, Romania and the UK.

The attacks mirrored the cyberattack that swept hundreds of supermarkets across France in October.

On Tuesday, France summoned Iran’s ambassador after accusing Tehran of a cyberattack that disabled refrigerators in hundreds of supermarkets.⁠

Tehran rejected the French accusations as “baseless” and “hostile”; however, the October incident made Iran a suspect in Wednesday’s hoax bomb threat.

Some European officials suspect Russia of orchestrating the campaign to disrupt daily life in countries supporting Ukraine after Moscow’s full-scale invasion.

Russia denies the accusation and describes it as a smear campaign.

articles.title: Nayib Buekele’s fight in Haiti: New hope, or greater havoc?
articles.summary: Bukele has emerged as a prominent global figure in the fight against gangs and organized crime.
articles.body:
The crisis in Haiti has fueled fatigue and frustration within the international community. Neither the Organization of American States nor the United Nations has been able to reverse this human tragedy. No superpower has been willing to put boots on the ground. Yet in March 2024, the president of the smallest country in Central America, El Salvador’s Nayib Bukele, declared his readiness to take on the challenge: “ We can fix it .”

Bukele has emerged as a prominent global figure in the fight against gangs and organized crime. He transformed his own country, once the most dangerous country in the Americas, into the safest nation in the Western Hemisphere. In 2025, El Salvador recorded 1.3 homicides per 100,000 inhabitants.

In January of 2025 , El Salvador joined U.N. security efforts in Haiti. Then, in October, four aviation technicians were captured by Haitian gangs. Bukele called for the immediate release of the technicians, sending 2,000 more troops to Haiti and issuing a strong ultimatum: “We have already finished the gangs in El Salvador, and we can finish with you too.”

Haiti is not a regular country with gangs. It has a nationwide gang coalition, which functions much like an army, under the name of Viv Ansanm (Live Together). In 2025, the group was designated by the U.S. as an international terrorist organization.

According to the United Nations , at least 5,519 people were killed and 2,608 were injured in Haiti between March 2025, and Jan. 15, 2026 in gang-related violence, with 1.4 million internally displaced.

Bukele sent a message to the Haitian people : “We can help you defeat them, but we are not invaders. We are people with the same courage as you. We must stand up, take back control of our communities, and bring those who are making us endure all this pain, all this suffering, under our control.”

The arrival of Bukele’s troops has brought a sense of hope to Haitians after years of suffering, death and neglect. They were received with chants of “We are Bukele” and “Long live Bukele!” Hatian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aime thanked Bukele and said , “He understands our fight. He came to stand on the side of the Haitian people.”

Since the arrival of elite troops from El Salvador, the situation has begun to shift. For the first time, a gang leader has been captured: Jean Saint Louis, alias “Kenken,” was arrested by Salvadoran forces and the Haitian Coast Guard. Meanwhile, last week, Mathias Saintil — a member of the “Boston Gang” — was killed , and Wilson Joseph, the top leader of the 400 Mawozo gang, has requested U.N. mediation , expressing concern over the arrival of the Salvadoran troops.

Bukele faces several challenges. Unlike in El Salvador, Haiti lacks the support of a strong government, a functional prosecutor’s office, a robust judiciary or a high-security prison system in Haiti. Furthermore, he faces a massive coalition of gangs and is at a numerical disadvantage. Added to this are the differences in terrain, language and culture — an entirely unfamiliar environment.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio has also noted that security and coordination in Haiti are key components. He said that “de-confliction” is essential.

“What you can’t have is gang suppression force running into Salvadorian soldiers and shooting at each other because they think the other side are gang members,” he said . “You’ll need a lot of strong coordination, because they’re operating alongside one another.”

Amnesty International has also expressly called on the government of Haiti and the government of El Salvador to respect human rights. “The vast majority of Salvadoran military personnel recently deployed to Haiti are not part of the Gang Suppression Force, authorized by the UN Security Council, and therefore fall outside the mandate and monitoring mechanisms of the United Nations Support Office in Haiti.”

The truth is, the crisis in Haiti is far more complex than the gang situation in El Salvador. Currently, Haiti is home to the U.N. Gang Suppression Force , in addition to forces working for security contractor Erik Prince, Bukele’s troops, the Haitian police and military and the massive gang coalition known as Viv Ansanm.

Bukele’s efforts in Haiti face a challenge of epic proportions, like a dark mirror of a new Vietnam in the Caribbean. Only time will tell whether his presence in Haiti brings change or chaos, a new hope or a greater havoc.

Arturo McFields is an exiled journalist, former Nicaraguan ambassador to the Organization of American States, and a former member of the Norwegian Peace Corps. He is an alumnus of the National Defense University’s Security and Defense Seminar and the Harvard Leadership course.

articles.title: Government solar farm rejection 'big blow' to Oxfordshire, say developers
articles.summary: The government refused permission for the £800m Botley West solar farm in Oxfordshire on Tuesday.
articles.body:
A government decision to reject proposals for one of Europe's largest solar farms is a "big blow" to the local area, the developers behind the scheme have said.

The £800m Botley West solar farm in Oxfordshire would have spread across more than 2,000 acres of land to the north and west of Oxford.

On Tuesday, the Secretary of State for Energy Security and Net Zero rejected the plans , saying they would cause "substantial" harm to greenbelt and heritage assets.

Mark Owen-Lloyd, director of the developers behind the scheme Photovolt Development Partners (PVDP), said the decision was "disappointing".

"The overwhelming local feedback I got was support, and we have been working on this for five years," Owen-Lloyd said.

"The decision of the Secretary of State is a big blow to Oxfordshire."

PVDP previously said the project was crucial to meeting the UK's climate and energy security goals, and could power the equivalent of 330,000 homes.

But in its ruling the government said it did not do enough to mitigate negative impacts on the landscape.

Consent was also refused as the site would have "adverse impacts on aviation safety" presenting an unacceptable risk to public safety.

The developer now has six weeks to launch a judicial review. Owen-Lloyd said the firm had "a decision to make in the coming days".

"If we apply to judicial review and succeed we could come back and reframe this project, so we might reduce it [in size] or reapply," he said.

"But we've spent a lot of time on this - maybe it's a moment to move on and do one of the other eight projects that we've got in the UK," he added.

The government decision followed several years of consultations, with the proposals proving controversial across Oxfordshire.

Bicester and Woodstock MP Calum Miller has been a consistent critic of the plans and said he was "delighted" the the government had made the "right decision for our area" in refusing it permission.

"This was a proposal that could have done so much better," the Liberal Democrat said.

"We desperately need a move to renewables, but throughout this process the developers were greedy in the amount of land that they wanted and they just didn't listen to the local communities."

articles.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Tuesday the U.S. and China should have a “more balanced” trading relationship, days after President Trump said he expects to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping later this month. “The U.S. trade imbalance with China has long been a source of friction,” Bessent said at a gala hosted by the…
articles.body:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Tuesday the U.S. and China should have a “more balanced” trading relationship , days after President Trump said he expects to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping later this month.

“The U.S. trade imbalance with China has long been a source of friction,” Bessent said at a gala hosted by the National Committee on U.S.-China Relations.

“Let me state firmly and unequivocally tonight that as we work toward a more balanced relationship, our objective is to de-risk, not to decouple,” he added later.

America’s trade deficit with China reached a 20-year low last year, as U.S. firms imported $202.7 billion more in goods from the Asian country than Chinese businesses brought in from the U.S., according to data from the Census Bureau.

The U.S. has had a trade deficit with China for decades, but it has grown since the turn of the century.

Bessent said Tuesday the American economy “has grown too dependent” on foreign supply, adding that China’s economy “has become increasingly reliant” on foreign demand.

“In other words, the United States must produce more of what we consume, while China must consume more of what it produces,” the Treasury secretary remarked. “Working together, we can strengthen both of our economies without perpetuating the imbalances between them.”

Trump said Sunday he expects to meet with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin next week at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China.

“One of the meetings, I think, will be with President Putin and President Xi,” he told reporters in Florida on Sunday.

The president added he will discuss “denuclearization” with his Chinese and Russian counterparts. The U.S., China and Russia hold more than 80 percent of the world’s available nuclear warheads, according to data from the Federation of American Scientists.

Trump hosted Xi in September, with U.S. and Chinese officials agreeing before the summit to extend the trade truce between the two countries until Jan. 10, 2027.

The deal, which the two leaders agreed to last year, resulted in lower U.S. tariffs on Chinese exports and China suspending its export controls on rare earth metals. Officials from the two countries also agreed in September to lower tariffs on $30 billion worth of products .

Bessent said Tuesday the administration intends to “advance a fair and reciprocal relationship with China,” as two months remain before the two countries must either extend the truce again or reach a larger trade deal.

“After decades of imbalance, we are restoring a spirit of reciprocity for the benefit of both of our peoples,” he added.

articles.title: Inside Holocaust memorial in heart of Arab world as founder reveals what changed everything
articles.summary: Inside Dubai's Crossroads of Civilizations Museum, founder Ahmed Obaid Al Mansoori reveals how a temporary Holocaust tribute became a permanent gallery.
articles.body: DUBAI, United Arab Emirates — In a historic house near Dubai Creek, a small gallery commemorating the six million Jews murdered in the Holocaust stands alongside collections exploring Islamic civilization, Emirati heritage and the history of Palestine and the Holy Land. The Holocaust exhibition at the privately owned Crossroads of Civilizations Museum is among the first permanent displays of its kind in the Arab world. Opened in May 2021, less than a year after the UAE normalized relations with Israel through the Abraham Accords, it has become a symbol of the Emirates' approach to religious coexistence. During a recent visit to the museum, Fox News Digital saw displays documenting Nazi persecution, including a life-size image of the boy from the famous Warsaw Ghetto photograph, his hands raised in surrender. The gallery also tells the stories of Muslims who rescued Jews during the Holocaust, including Egyptian physician Mohammed Helmy, who sheltered Jews from Nazi persecution in Berlin. US-BACKED ISRAEL-MOROCCO DEAL DEEPENS ABRAHAM ACCORDS AMID GROWING REGIONAL THREATS But the story behind the exhibition is as personal as the objects it preserves. In an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital, museum founder Ahmed Obaid Al Mansoori, a former member of the UAE's Federal National Council, explained that his passion for collecting historical artifacts began in childhood, when he inherited family manuscripts and objects from his grandparents. DOMINICAN REPUBLIC JOINS GLOBAL FIGHT AGAINST ANTISEMITISM WITH LANDMARK MOVE He began collecting systematically in 1989, eventually establishing a private museum in his home in 2006. Dubai authorities later provided a historic building to accommodate his growing collection, which opened to the public in 2014. The Holocaust gallery came much later. 9/11 MUSEUM UNVEILS EXHIBITION FOR GENERATION TOO YOUNG TO REMEMBER THE ATTACKS: 'CALLED EVERYBODY TO LEAD' Al Mansoori said two experiences inspired him. The first was a visit to the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum in Washington during the 1990s, where he was deeply moved by the message that the Holocaust was a tragedy with lessons for all humanity. The second was a conversation with an American Jewish acquaintance who expressed fear about rising antisemitism in the United States. Initially, he dismissed her concerns. But after encountering antisemitic imagery circulating during a period of unrest in the U.S., he reconsidered. "I realized I was wrong," he said. He turned to Jewish friends and colleagues to organize a Holocaust remembrance event in Dubai in 2021. CHRISTIAN LEADERS HOLD EMERGENCY SUMMIT IN JERUSALEM TO CONFRONT GLOBAL RISE IN ANTISEMITISM "The beauty about this Holocaust gallery was built by Arabs, by Jews, and by Christians," he told Fox News Digital, describing the international team that helped create the exhibition. What began as a commemorative initiative became something much larger. At the opening, Al Mansoori said, he was struck by the positive response from visitors, including residents of the UAE and people from elsewhere in the region. He also encountered criticism, but concluded that the gallery should become a permanent part of the museum. "I thought it was very beautiful, very important. And it must stay," he recalled. The exhibition formally opened on May 26, 2021, attended by the Israeli and German ambassadors to the UAE, according to The National's coverage at the time. TRUMP CALLS ON ARAB NATIONS TO SIGN ABRAHAM ACCORDS Yet Al Mansoori's vision extends beyond Holocaust remembrance. In another section of the museum, historical maps of Palestine appear alongside Jewish manuscripts, photographs and documents illustrating the region's overlapping histories. "You have the maps from the Israeli perspective. You have the map from the Palestinian perspective," he said, explaining why he deliberately brings different historical narratives into the same space. He recalled a visit by rabbis in August 2020, when Muslim, Jewish and Christian guests prayed alongside one another at the museum, each according to their own traditions. For Al Mansoori, the purpose is not to erase religious or political differences, but to make it possible for people to respect one another despite them. "It's how to learn to be comfortable being yourself next to others. And others must be also comfortable to be next to you," he said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP As war and political tensions continue to divide the Middle East, Al Mansoori believes the museum offers a different way to confront the region's painful history: not by avoiding it, but by allowing visitors to encounter histories and experiences beyond their own.

articles.title: Who is Alice Huang, alleged spy who reportedly had affair with Nvidia CEO?
articles.summary: Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang has entered the spotlight in the recent days following reports of her intimate relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and allegations of her being a spy. A recent New York Times report claimed that American authorities discovered Alice Huang illegally smuggled advanced AI chips into China while developing a “close relationship”…
articles.body:
Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang has entered the spotlight in the recent days following reports of her intimate relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and allegations of her being a spy .

A recent New York Times report claimed that American authorities discovered Alice Huang illegally smuggled advanced AI chips into China while developing a “close relationship” with the Nvidia co-founder.

The reports prompted an independent investigation by Nvidia. The company announced Tuesday that it retained a former acting U.S. attorney, Joon H. Kim, and his firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct the investigation. In a previous statement, the company’s board said it had “no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets” were compromised by Jensen Huang’s relationship with the accused Chinese spy.

Here is what to know about Alice Huang and the scandal.

Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was previously a Chinese finance executive before she assumed a leadership position at a Singapore-based cloud-computing company Megaspeed International, according to reports from The Associated Press and Reuters .

In early 2023, Alice Huang became a controlling shareholder in Megaspeed with all the company’s shares transferred to Huang Le Limited, a company registered in the British Virgin Islands, the AP reported.

However, by November 2023, she was no longer a director at the company with all her shares transferred to Tan Yong Pong, a Singaporean businessman. In May this year, a report from short seller Culper Research cited a Megaspeed employee who said Alice Huang was still involved in the company’s operations.

Megaspeed is listed as an official cloud partner of Nvidia, Reuters reported. Last, year, the company was under investigation over allegations that it was helping Chinese customers get advanced Nvidia chips which are subject to U.S. export restrictions, the reports said.

Before Megaspeed, Huang held senior positions, such as deputy general manager, executive director and member of the investment committee, at Chinese investment firm Shanghai Hexi Investment Management, according to both reports. Prior to that, she worked at HSBC’s Hong Kong private banking arm and CITIC Securities, headquartered in China.

What are the allegations surrounding Alice Huang and Jensen Huang?

The Times report last month alleged that U.S. officials concluded Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence asset who was passing information to Beijing, all while developing a relationship with the Nvidia CEO. China denied the claims that she is a spy, with its foreign ministry saying the allegation is “unsubstantiated.”

“It is nothing but smears against China,” the foreign ministry added, according to the AP.

The Nvidia CEO recently acknowledged that he has been unfaithful to his wife, adding “My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry,” according to a report from Bloomberg .

He has been called to appear by GOP lawmakers in a joint, closed-door briefing on Nov. 18 to address concerns regarding Nvidia’s security protocols and his interactions with the alleged spy.

The Times reported on Tuesday, citing people with knowledge of the situation, that President Trump was told on Air Force One while traveling to China in May that the U.S. had obtained sensitive intelligence showing the Nvidia CEO was in a relationship with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy.
